newsitem.title: HONG KONG: INTERVIEW - CITIC Pac seeks new projects.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - CITIC Pac seeks new projects.

text.p: CITIC Pacific Ltd is seeking to invest in China infrastructure and Hong Kong properties after pocketing cash from the sale of 7.74 percent of Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, CITIC Pacific managing director Henry Fan said on Monday.
"In China, for example, we are looking at Phase III project in Ligang (power station)," Fan told Reuters.
The phase three coal-fired power station in China's Jiangsu province would have two 660 megawatt generators, he added.
"It's huge and this is one project which it is now in a better position to undertake with our gearing now substantially lower," Fan said.
CITIC Pacific has agreed in principle to sell its stake in Hongkong Telecom for a total of HK$11.4 billion.
The Hong Kong-based conglomerate would net a profit of around HK$3.6 billion after expenses from the deal, he said.

Fan said that the deal would cut CITIC Pacific's gearing based on asset values to 18 percent, from 30 percent previously. The total investment in Ligang's phase three project was still being worked out, he said.
CITIC Pacific has 56.31 percent of the Ligang Power Station, which has two 350 MW generators each in Phases I and II.
Fan said Phase I of Ligang would be operating soon, with the first generator of Phase II starting by the end of the year.
"In terms of other infrastructural projects, we are in discussion with several major cities of China with regard to the possibility of undertaking some projects," he said.
In Hong Kong, it will be involved with China Light and Power Co Ltd (CLP) in both Hong Kong and China after paying HK$16.25 billion for 20 percent of the Hong Kong-based utility.
"China Light is definitely one area we are now spending a lot of time on and there are several fronts," Fan said.
Fan said the company was helping CLP with its Shandong power plant joint venture. "I think we are almost there now," he said.
CITIC Pacific is an investment arm of China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC) which is directly controlled by China's State Council.
CLP said in January that the State Council had approved its proposed power plant project in China's Shandong province.
It was still awaiting the green light from the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation before a joint venture company could be formed.
He said CITIC Pacific was talking to CLP on how to change its Hong Kong power business to better suit the changing environment.
"We are also assisting China Light with our property expertise with the possibility of maximising the property redevelopment potential of China Light," he said.
CITIC Pacific was also discussing some new property development projects in Hong Kong, he added.
Asked about the geographical spread of CITIC Pacific's businesses, Fan said: "I would see a parallel development in both Hong Kong and China. -- Hong Kong newsroom (852) 2843 6369
